questions.title: The tall tiered columns at 大水法 and 观水法

evidence.title: 御製 題澤蘭堂
evidence.excerpt_zh:
題澤蘭堂
書堂號澤蘭樸斵謝青丹芸帙堪永日藤窻避薄寒蕪情報韶意水法列竒觀（堂北為西洋水法處盖縁乾隆十八年西洋博爾都噶里雅國）（來京朝貢聞彼處以水法為竒觀因念中國地大物博水法不過工巧之一端遂命住京之西洋人郎世寧造）（為此法俾來使至此瞻仰前嵗□咭唎國使臣等至京朝貢亦令閲看深為歎服昨冬廣東督臣長麟撫臣朱）（珪奏荷蘭國使臣嘚□等以今嵗為朕御極六十年大慶懇請来京朝賀鑒其數萬里外慕化悃誠因允其請）（已即於臈月到京新正並與朝賀宴賞節間令於是處觀看水法使知朕所嘉者逺人嚮化之誠若其任土作）（貢則中國之大何竒不有初不以為貴也）洋使賀正至逺瀛合俾看
evidence.summary: The one imperial statement found on the European water works. Qianlong's note says the 西洋水法 stands north of 澤蘭堂; after a Portuguese embassy of 乾隆十八年 (1753) he had 郎世寧 Castiglione build it to show envoys; British envoys saw it in the 1790s, and the Dutch envoys at New Year 1795 were to see it. He adds that what he values is their coming, not their marvels.

evidence.title: Test of the claim that the fountains stopped when Benoist died in 1774
evidence.summary: Result: the common form of the claim is wrong in two ways. (1) The machines failed before Benoist died: the wheel broke in 1763 and windlasses replaced it. (2) The fountains did not stop: reports of 1786 and 1789 have men filling the reservoir a day or two before a visit so that the water could play for the emperor (Bourgeois); wicker buckets from the river (Amiot); pipes repaired 1794, Dutch envoys meant to see the 水法 in early 1795 (E0185); machines scrapped 1795, but 嘉庆's poems of 1796-98 still mention water sent by machine: poetry, weak. Holding: after 1763 or so the fountains ran on occasion with stored water, carried by labour.

evidence.title: 远瀛观: 嘉庆三年 poem of the Jiaqing Emperor
evidence.date: 嘉庆三年 (1798), date from the compilation
evidence.excerpt_zh: 引机运水石池注，溅玉喷珠万斛雄。敬识圣皇声教广，流沙西海尽同风。
evidence.summary: Jiaqing, 1798: machine-raised water fills a stone basin, with jets of spray: a dated witness that the fountains worked.

evidence.title: Plate XV: 大水法 Da Shuifa
evidence.excerpt_other: au milieu duquel est un cerf en pied, dont le bois lance de l'eau par chacun de ses andouillers:
evidence.summary: Two high water pyramids. A mask at the top of the central piece fills a shell basin, then six basins in cascade, then a large basin with a stag whose antlers spout, hounds spouting at it from both sides.

evidence.title: Engraving 15: 大水法 Da Shuifa
evidence.excerpt_other: On the right and left stood excessively tall pyramidal fountains surrounded by numerous small jets.
evidence.summary: Two tall pyramids with small jets; a pool in the middle where jets played on animals, birds and fish, before the carved terrace of 远瀛观. Plate p.156: ruins in 1924.

evidence.title: Detail gain, 3 plates against the catalogue thumbs
evidence.locator: crops cmp08, cmp12, cmp15, cmp01 in palace_r6_tmp_plates
evidence.summary: Same regions at 900 px. Plate 8 (P0048): window lattice, shading hatch and baluster ornament resolve, thumb showed them as texture. Plate 12 (P0052): door panel pattern and urn outlines clear. Plate 15 (P0055): water drops and fountain tiers separate, thumb mashes them. Original is 2.6 times wider than the thumb. Plate 1 Chester Beatty against Palace Museum: 2.7 times wider again and far darker: roof tile, hatch and capitals sharp.

evidence.title: Notice on Benoist: the first fountain
evidence.excerpt_other: La machine hydraulique & le premier jet-d'eau ne furent finis qu'à la fin de l'automne.
evidence.summary: French text behind S02 p.139. Autumn of 1747 or just after. Which building is not stated.

evidence.title: Xiyang Lou: origin, 1747
evidence.excerpt_other: The hydraulic machine and the first fountain were finished at the end of autumn.
evidence.summary: From the 1775 life of Benoist in Lettres édifiantes vol. xxiv: Qianlong saw a picture of a fountain in 1747, Benoist made a model, and the emperor resolved to build a European palace. Castiglione drew the plans with Benoist; Benoist designed the fountains and the "water castles" and trained the workmen. He worked on fountains for about twelve years. Which fountain came first is not stated.

evidence.title: Written then-and-now captions on Morrison photographs
evidence.summary: Compares about nine 1930s photographs with today in words, not with new pictures. Claims the single-arch gate remnant on the south of 海晏堂 stood in the Republican years and has now collapsed, and the two arch frames at 远瀛观 have mostly fallen. Unverified user writing.

evidence.title: 圆明园五朝御制诗文集注 v4, editors' note on 西洋楼
evidence.summary: The editors walk the strip from west to east with completion dates and plaques: 谐奇趣 1751, 养雀笼 1759, then the fountains and the perspective walls, with their mechanical details. They put the whole at about 2% of the gardens.

evidence.title: 西洋楼水法图
evidence.locator: 国家图书馆善本部 none shown
evidence.summary: Plan of the Xiyang Lou waterworks across its dozen sites; the record shows no shelf number. No image here; the site may ask a small payment for the full record.

evidence.title: Teng Gu's preface on the photographs and plan
evidence.locator: pp.3-5 of the preface, djvu pages 5-7
evidence.summary: Teng Gu says the photographs and the plan belonged to Ernst Boerschmann and were taken and drawn by Ohlmer, a customs official in Tianjin who lived in Beijing 1867-1879 and whose collection went to the Hildesheim museum. He argues they are earlier than those in Favier's Péking (1897), Combaz 1909, Perzynski 1920 and Münsterberg 1912, naming pages he compared. Fig. 13 is a recent photograph by Zhou Zuanwu; fig. 15 is copied from Favier p.264.

evidence.title: Three plans by Antoine Durand: 1984 from Jin Xun at 1/500 inside Adam's 1/10000; 1985 from a survey of the whole site; 1987 fountain area from 128 surveyed points with a manual survey of all surface parts
evidence.summary: The only published method statement for an on-site survey of the whole strip. Only excavation could fix the east fence of the gardens and the east edge of the basin. The west edge of the 线法山 gate and the ramp fix the geometry. See R0139-R0143. Plans without a printed scale in the copy I read.

evidence.title: Yangshi Lei plan cards on 梦回圆明园: 勤政殿平面图, 西峰秀色总平面图, 安佑宫室内布置图, 映清斋平面图, 绮春园宫门区平面图, 敷春堂殿平面图, 敷春堂东南所平面图, 涵秋馆地盘图, 四宜书屋(绮春园)平面图, 河道泊岸总平面图, 长春园样式雷河道图, 西洋楼水法图, 御制廓然大公八景诗图
evidence.summary: Titles seen in the index, drawings not opened. Pattern: https://www.mhymy.com/dasl/ysltd/<id>.html.

evidence.title: 圆明园遗址考古今年推进至大水法, 浙江在线
evidence.summary: 养雀笼 Yangque Long: 1,000 m2 cleared in 2015, showing foundations that combine 三合土 lime concrete with brick and stone. 大水法 and 远瀛观 were next, about 2,000 m2 planned for 2016, with the stated aim of learning how imperial buildings were founded, which standing buildings cannot show.

evidence.title: 西洋楼区域考古勘探报告
evidence.locator: mhymy 档案史料 12205, free part
evidence.summary: Report's opening: the strip runs 860 m east-west, up to 300 m wide in the west and 65 m at its narrowest, about 70,000 m2, built 1747-1783. A central axis divides it into about five sections, each with its own north-south axis, thirteen units from 谐奇趣 to 线法墙. Survey results are paywalled.

reconstructions.title: 3D技术复现“万园之园”: 北京大学 stone scanning
reconstructions.archive: 圆明园管理处; 北京大学考古文博学院
reconstructions.why: The park and Peking University's School of Archaeology and Museology record the carved stones by 3D scan, photogrammetry and panorama, at 大水法, 观水法, 远瀛观, 海晏堂 and pieces now on the Peking University campus. This is the nearest thing found to a 'Peking University Digital Yuanmingyuan'. It says over 10 sites have been dug since the 1990s.

reconstructions.title: Plan de l'aire du buffet d'eau (Fig. 3 in S603), Jin Xun's drawing
reconstructions.creator: 金勋 Jin Xun
reconstructions.why: As Jin Xun's Fig. 2. S603 survey: this area really runs 110 m east-west, not 90 as Jin Xun drew it; 线法山 west gate not centred; side walls of the water theatre placed in a way that yields no perspective.
reconstructions.caveat: A modern reconstruction drawing, not a Qing document.
reconstructions.licence: none stated; S597 gives the author dates 1881-1976 in one place and 1883-1976 in another

reconstructions.title: Fig. 4, Plan d'ensemble (plan de restitution 1985)
reconstructions.creator: Antoine Durand
reconstructions.archive: Mission Palais d'Ete, under Michele Pirazzoli-t'Serstevens
reconstructions.why: Three stages: 1984 plan from Jin Xun's plan fragments in Adam 1936, on the 1:10,000 park plan at 1:500, corrected by site readings and engravings; 1985 plan from a survey of the whole site, with general dimensions and setting of each building; water theatre from a Lei family drawing, Alimoff photo for the west basin of 海晏堂, engravings for planting.
reconstructions.licence: none stated on the Persee page

reconstructions.title: Fig. 5, Plan de l'aire du buffet d'eau (plan de restitution 1987)
reconstructions.creator: Antoine Durand
reconstructions.why: Walks set from surviving central paving, 128 points by angle plus hand survey of what lay on the surface; obelisks and mushroom fountains inspired by the engravings; basin outline from surviving kerbs, symmetric; seven of thirteen animal bases located.
reconstructions.licence: none stated on the Persee page

twins.name: 特里亚农 水台 Buffet d'Eau, Grand Trianon
twins.relation: Comparable: same court, era or type
twins.tells: Tiered marble wall of water; shell ornament
twins.basis: S415 p.22, quoting the Lettres édifiantes (t. XIII per Rabreau; S02 pp.158-159 cites vol. xxiv p.421, cf. S257): the great water piece «soutiendrait le parallèle» with those of Versailles and St Cloud, and from his throne the emperor sees two great water pyramids. S02: pyramids, carved pool edges, statues, shell ornament in both. S420: the Trianon Buffet d'Eau is by Hardouin-Mansart, 1702, «Italian-inspired», restoration begun 2022.

facts.label: English
facts.value: Ta Shui Fa, the Great Fountains

facts.label: Built
facts.value: After the Portuguese embassy of 乾隆十八年 (1753), per Qianlong's note, built by 郎世寧 Castiglione

facts.label: Destroyed
facts.value: Looted and burnt 1860; stone ruins stayed, further damage 1900 and after (S02 pp.142,218)

facts.label: Position
facts.value: 40.01221, 116.30660. S850;S01, moved in Round 6: on the ruin, research/xiyanglou/boxes.csv

facts.label: Lead on its size, from a modern study, not used in the model
facts.value: Water-buffet area 110 x 60 m, level drop 1.30 m at the banks, hedges about 2.50 m; composition of the rockwork and throne about 50 m long; twin basins 18 m in diameter, 62 m between centres (S603, p. 127).

facts.label: Note
facts.value: Copper engraving no. 15 per S02. Tall pyramids and animal figures (S02 p.156). S06 10 hounds and a stag. Round 6 replaced frontage 20.0 m. Round 6 replaced depth 3.0 m.
